Subject: Post-call recap: dedicated pool runbook, SLAs, and scaling intents

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same view and we can close the open items.

Key pain points you shared:
- P1: Production latency spikes during end-of-day batch scoring (90–120s currently for long sequences).
- P2: Compliance requirement for tenant isolation and audit logs (SOC2 + regional data residency concerns).
- P3: Need predictable throughput for triage/urgency use cases during clinical hours, with occasional bursts for nightly processing.

Goals you confirmed:
1) Dedicated GPU pool with single-tenant isolation for PHI workflows.
2) 99th-percentile latency target of <120ms for 512 tokens interactive calls; nightly batch throughput of ~200k tokens/min.
3) On-call runbook and SLA fallback behavior documented for both latency and availability incidents.

What we propose next (summary of action items):
- Redwood: deliver an ops runbook draft that covers alerting thresholds, escalation steps, and automated fallback to a compatible lower-cost model variant. See attached: medoptima_mop_v1.pdf (ops playbook sketch).
- Redwood infra: provide a sizing proposal showing baseline reserved GPUs + burst capacity and an annotated topology (inference-topology.png).
- MedOptima: confirm compliance constraints (preferred KMS, retention window) and procurement timeline.

Questions we need back from you to finalize the proposal:
- Which cloud region must the reserved pool live in (us-east-1 vs us-west-2)?
- Who should be the primary on-call contact for first-level escalations (name + phone)?
- Do you have a preferred SLA clause that procurement needs (termination rights / credit model)?

Next meeting: propose Wed 10 Mar, 10:00–10:45 PT to review the runbook and SLA draft. I’ll put a calendar hold once you confirm the time.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Elena — quick technical note on the KV-cache fallback question. Two practical levers we recommend and can include in the runbook:

1) Adaptive prefix caching: keep warm caches for the top 200 clinical prompts during business hours; fall back to a quantized model variant for cold misses.
2) Burst lanes: pre-warm a one-slot burst lane with a small standby VM+vGPU that can accept short-lived spikes and drain into the reserved pool. This reduces the tail latency without over-provisioning.

I attached a short SLA draft that includes a fallback credit model (see sla-draft-medoptima-2027.docx). The key behavioral trigger is: if sustained 95th-98th pct KV miss rate > X for 10m AND p99 latency > 500ms, Redwood will route new interactive traffic to the pre-warmed burst lane and notify on-call.

Happy to walk through the exact numbers on Wed.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
